messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Fluoxetine is FDA-approved to treat the following conditions:
Major depressive disorder (MDD) for acute and maintenance treatment in adults and children aged 8 years and older
Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) for acute and maintenance treatment in adults and children aged 7 years and older
Bulimia nervosa for acute and maintenance treatment of binge-eating and purging in adults with moderate to severe bulimia
Panic disorder for the treatment of panic attacks in adults
When used in combination with olanzapine, fluoxetine is also FDA-approved for:
Acute treatment of depressive episodes associated with Bipolar I disorder (depressive episodes) in adults and children aged 10 years and older
Treatment-resistant depression for adults who have not responded to at least two adequate antidepressant trials
Fluoxetine alone is not approved for bipolar I depressive episodes or treatment-resistant depression.
Olanzapine must be used in combination for these indications.
Triples: [["Fluoxetine", "fda approved to treat", "Major depressive disorder (MDD)"], ["Fluoxetine", "used for acute and maintenance treatment in", "adults"], ["Fluoxetine", "used for acute and maintenance treatment in", "children aged 8 years and older"], ["Fluoxetine", "fda approved to treat", "Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD)"], ["Fluoxetine", "used for acute and maintenance treatment in", "children aged 7 years and older"], ["Fluoxetine", "fda approved to treat", "Bulimia nervosa"], ["Fluoxetine", "used for acute and maintenance treatment of", "binge-eating and purging in adults with moderate to severe bulimia"], ["Fluoxetine", "fda approved to treat", "Panic disorder"], ["Fluoxetine", "used for treatment of", "panic attacks in adults"], ["Fluoxetine", "used in combination with", "olanzapine"], ["Fluoxetine", "fda approved for acute treatment of", "depressive episodes associated with Bipolar I disorder (depressive episodes) in adults and children aged 10 years and older"], ["Fluoxetine", "fda approved for", "Treatment-resistant depression for adults who have not responded to at least two adequate antidepressant trials"], ["Fluoxetine alone", "not approved for", "bipolar I depressive episodes"], ["Fluoxetine alone", "not approved for", "treatment-resistant depression"], ["Olanzapine", "must be used in combination with", "Fluoxetine for these indications"]]
Relations: ["fda approved for", "fda approved for acute treatment of", "fda approved to treat", "must be used in combination with", "not approved for", "used for acute and maintenance treatment in", "used for acute and maintenance treatment of", "used for treatment of", "used in combination with"]
Answer:

completion:
fda approved for: The subject drug is officially approved by the FDA for the medical indication or use specified by the object entity.  
fda approved for acute treatment of: The subject drug is officially approved by the FDA for the acute treatment of the medical condition specified by the object entity.  
fda approved to treat: The subject drug is officially approved by the FDA to treat the medical condition specified by the object entity.  
must be used in combination with: The subject drug must be used in conjunction with the drug or substance specified by the object entity for the indicated medical condition.  
not approved for: The subject drug is not officially approved by the FDA for the medical condition or use specified by the object entity.  
used for acute and maintenance treatment in: The subject drug is used for both acute and maintenance treatment of the patient population or condition specified by the object entity.  
used for acute and maintenance treatment of: The subject drug is used for both acute and maintenance treatment of the medical condition or symptom specified by the object entity.  
used for treatment of: The subject drug is used for the treatment of the medical condition or symptom specified by the object entity.  
used in combination with: The subject drug is used in conjunction with the drug or substance specified by the object entity.
